newsitem.title: ESTONIA: LITHUANIA-BRAZAUSKAS SAYS MAY NOT RUN-REPORT.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA-BRAZAUSKAS SAYS MAY NOT RUN-REPORT.

text.p: Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas gave his strongest hint to date that he may not run in December's presidential election, the Estonian newspaper Sonumileht reported on Monday.
The paper quoted Brazauskas as saying that age and his political past were factors leading him to seriously consider calling it quits.
"I think it's enough. First of all there is my age," the paper quoted Brazauskas as saying in an interview.

"I also look critically at my political biography...I was the first secretary of Lithuania's Communist Party...but where in Europe is there such a president left? I am the only one left," Brazauskas said.
But he added that he had made no final decision yet.
Brazauskas, 64, has been president since February 1993.
Political analysts in Lithuania have not written him off yet, pointing out that he relishes the position and consistently tops opinion polls as the best man for the job.
